svg.title: The engine layer — an implied contract that nothing enforces

g.text: The engine layer — an implied contract that nothing enforces
TRUST BOUNDARY — dispatch on UNAUTHENTICATED input
POST /chat has no auth dependency (main.py:274-275); require_user() can never 401 (auth.py:95-97);
There is no ABC, no Protocol, no base class.
streaming protocol — checked by nothing at runtime
There is genuinely no interface object in this codebase.
independent declaration that can drift without a type error:
Nothing checks at runtime that an engine returns `str`, that it
emits `meta` at all, or that it emits it only once. The rule is
written in comments only (graph.py:32-35, agent.py:604, chat.py:103).
Signature drift — the contract's third parameter is not stable.
`emit` sits at position 3 in chat/sql/rag/report/agent, position 4
in vision (vision.py:66) and dataset (dataset.py:87), and position 5
the same knob keyword-only (search.py:460 vs chat.py:66, agent.py:631).
Because there is no Protocol, none of this is a type error — it is
only ever caught by the call site being written correctly by hand.
`vision.run_vision_engine` even accepts `history` and never reads it
(vision.py:69), so follow-up questions about an image reach the model
router.py — 2 swallowed exceptions, 0 log lines, no timeout.
`except Exception: pass` at router.py:121-122 and :130-131 hide
connection-refused, HTTP 400 window errors and read timeouts
identically. The only bound is the 300 s OpenAI client timeout
(llm.py:78) applied twice: a wedged router endpoint plus a wedged
`return "rag"` at router.py:133 — i.e. a total classifier outage
silently routes greetings into the vector-search engine.
There is no confidence score anywhere: `parse_route` returns a
orchestrate.decide runs on every text turn, unguarded.
and the same in `parse_plan` (:104-106) — no log, no retry, no
per-call timeout. It is awaited at main.py:412,
first `status` event is published at main.py:415, so a slow
router endpoint is indistinguishable from a hung request in the UI.
`_JSON_RE = \{.*\}` is greedy (:38) and, unlike router.py and
agent.py, this parser strips neither `<think>` blocks nor code
fences — two JSON objects in one reply silently downgrade the plan.
live_sf is a helper masquerading as an engine module.
It lives in `engines/` and is never routed — `sql.py:318-319`
imports it lazily on the `NoSuchTable` branch and `agent.py:291`
on a `salesforce` step. Both reach the
over HTTPS, so an engine failure mode escalates to a real CRM read.
`core/salesforce.py:123-131` does not wrap the token POST in `try`,
so a `ConnectError` escapes as a raw httpx exception — and
aborting the whole agent step chain on a network blip.
agent.py swallows per step and ships the raw exception to the browser.
`except Exception` at agent.py:387 turns any step failure into
`step.detail` (agent.py:388-392) — stack-adjacent text rendered in the UI.
`return_exceptions=True`, so a `CancelledError` on Stop aborts the
gather and leaves sibling coroutines running.
No timeout exists anywhere in the engine layer
over `engines/*.py` matches only url.py:36 and search.py:315/338.
The single bound is the 300 s client timeout (llm.py:78) with the
installed SDK's `DEFAULT_MAX_RETRIES == 2` ⇒ **900 s worst case per
LLM call**, and 24 lines of unreachable duplicate Salesforce branch
Blocking I/O inside `async def` — the layer-wide defect.
awaited-adjacent from async engines: dataset.py:97, url.py:88/93,
(report.py:117) — a weasyprint fetch of a remote resource hangs the
generation forever. The codebase knows the pattern: `net.py:121`
bypasses the graph for: agent, document(pdf),
5 terminal branches; falls through to live_sf on NoSuchTable
emit is the 4th parameter, not the 3rd
NO `emit` parameter · emits NOTHING · returns a route string
class Plan(agent: bool, search: bool, auto: bool)
NO `emit` · emits NOTHING · returns a dataclass, not str
NO `emit` · never on a route · not in graph.py, not in main.py
sync DuckDB on the event loop
blocking file I/O on the event loop
conforming engine or dispatcher (orchestrator / app logic)
`..|>` purple dashed = satisfies the implied shape
`..|>` red bold = "implements" it only loosely (emit moved)
`..>` red bold = declared in `engines/` but violates the contract
Solid arrow = in-process `await`; label gives protocol + payload + sync/async.
